TEXT_E:
Labour Party Manifesto 2005: Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision and record
- Purpose: “Forward, not back” – government’s duty is to provide opportunity and security for all, marrying economic dynamism with social justice and matching rights with responsibilities.
- Record since 1997: Longest period of growth; lowest unemployment/inflation for a generation; 2m more in work; minimum wage and tax credits raised living standards; poverty among children and pensioners reduced. Major investment in schools and NHS (more teachers, doctors, nurses; faster treatments; heart and cancer deaths down). Crime down ~30% with more police and new community powers. Aid doubled and UK leading on climate policy.

Economy and enterprise
- Maintain macro stability: 2% inflation target, fiscal rules, low debt; no rise in basic/top income tax; no VAT on essentials; efficiency savings to fund services.
- Jobs and skills: Target 80% employment; higher minimum wage; welfare-to-work and Incapacity Benefit reform; expand apprenticeships and FE; science/innovation strategy to lift R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014.
- Business and infrastructure: Competitive taxation; lighter, better regulation; support SMEs and entrepreneurship; £180bn+ public transport investment to 2015; rail upgrades, HS options, congestion solutions (incl. road pricing study); free off-peak bus travel for over-60s.

Education
- Personalised learning: More teachers/support staff; parental engagement; firm discipline.
- Primary: Sustain literacy/numeracy gains; enrich arts, sport, languages; upgrade buildings.
- Secondary: All schools to be independent specialist schools; at least 200 Academies by 2010; Building Schools for the Future modernises estates; expansion where demand/quality justify.
- 14–19: Strengthen vocational routes with specialised diplomas; EMAs; more apprenticeships/FE.
- Higher education: More places with variable fees capped at £3,000, grants and bursaries; aim 50% participation; research investment boosted.

Health and social care
- NHS investment to triple by 2008; referral-to-treatment max 18 weeks; patient choice of hospital; expand primary/community services and community hospitals; prudent use of independent sector for capacity; cut bureaucracy; tackle MRSA and improve hygiene; dentistry review.
- Public health: Better school meals, nutrition standards and labelling; restrict junk-food marketing to children; smoke-free workplaces/restaurants (limited exemptions); expand cessation services; health trainers.

Crime, security, migration
- Neighbourhood policing in every community; more CSOs; strong action on antisocial behaviour and alcohol-related disorder; youth justice reforms.
- Cut drug-driven crime with compulsory testing/treatment; new Serious Organised Crime Agency.
- Tougher gun/knife controls; reduce reoffending with supervision, tagging, NOMS.
- Victim-focused justice; corporate manslaughter law; ID cards to combat fraud/illegal working.
- Immigration: Points system favouring skills; English for settlement; biometric visas/e-passports; employer penalties; faster, fair asylum.

Families, housing, older people
- Halve child poverty by 2010 and end it in a generation via work, tax credits, Child Trust Fund.
- Universal childcare: Sure Start Children’s Centres nationwide; extended schools 8am–6pm; more help with childcare costs.
- Parental leave to nine months (aim a year); expand flexible working (including carers).
- Housing: Increase homeownership by up to 2m; raise stamp duty threshold; shared-ownership/right-to-buy style schemes; more and better social housing with choice-based lettings.
- Older people: Pension Credit; Winter Fuel Payments; free local bus travel; forge consensus on long-term pensions; end unjustified forced retirement before 65; individual care budgets.

International, environment, culture, democracy
- Europe: Lead reform; referendum on Constitutional Treaty; NATO central; euro only if tests met.
- Security and development: Counter terrorism/WMD; support Iraq/Afghanistan transitions; Middle East peace; maintain nuclear deterrent; UN/G8 leadership on Africa and climate; reach 0.7% ODA by 2013; fairer trade.
- Environment: Clean neighbourhoods, higher recycling, brownfield building, sustainable homes, Marine Act; long-term CO2 cuts (−20% by 2010; −60% by 2050).
- Culture/sport: Free national museums; broaden participation; facility upgrades; 2012 Olympics legacy; BBC Trust and digital switchover 2008–2012.
- Democracy: More neighbourhood powers; stronger, freer local government; mayoral options; council tax restraint; further devolution; complete Lords reform; Single Equality Act and Equality & Human Rights Commission.

TEXT_G:
UKIP Manifesto 2005 – Summary

Core aim
- Leave the European Union to restore sovereignty, lawmaking and accountability to Westminster and local communities. Replace EU membership with trade and cooperation agreements. Introduce citizen-initiated referendums nationally and locally (triggered if 5% of the electorate sign within six months).

Exit plan
- Repeal the European Communities Act, end UK payments to the EU, reassert supremacy of UK law, and take an independent seat in global bodies. Two-year transition to review, repeal or replace EU-derived regulations and rebuild UK policies for farming and fishing.

Economy and regulation
- Trade: Maintain EU market access via bilateral deals; deepen global trade (NAFTA, Commonwealth, WTO).  
- Deregulation: Scrap or slim EU-driven rules, prioritising relief for small businesses.  
- Budget: Redirect net EU payments (c. £1bn/year) to raise state pensions by £2/week. Temporarily increase borrowing by £3bn/year (deficit up to ~6% of GDP) to fund immediate tax cuts and defence.  
- Tax: Immediate measures—halve council tax for all householders; scrap the 10% income tax band; reinstate pension fund dividend tax credits; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500,000. Long term—simplify by replacing VAT with a wholesale sales tax, merge National Insurance with income tax, consider a flat tax.

Health and welfare
- NHS: End central micromanagement and targets; restore local control and the “matron” model; scrap Strategic Health Authorities; expand GP hours; prioritise clinical judgment; consider complementary private insurance; remove EU limits (e.g., Working Time Directive; supplement rules).  
- Social security: Simplify and reduce means-testing to encourage work and saving; sceptical of “make-work” schemes.  
- Pensions: Immediate rise of £2/week; restore dividend tax credits; unfreeze pensions for UK expatriates. Long-term sustainability through more saving/longer working lives (not immigration).

Education
- Schools: More autonomy; scrap SATs and the QCA; empower heads on exclusions; support specialisation and limited selection; promote sports and trips; expand assisted places, vouchers/tax rebates for private options.  
- Universities: Reduce low-quality courses; fully fund high-standard ones; abolish top-up fees; restore maintenance grants; end student loans; charge EU students full fees; expand technical colleges.

Law, order, and immigration
- Policing: Local accountability; cut paperwork; stronger magistrates; credible sentencing; more prison capacity; protect homeowners. Reject EU Corpus Juris.  
- Immigration: Aim near-zero net migration; points-based work permits; equal rules for EU/non-EU; tighter family reunion; restore embarkation controls; “Britishness” tests; safe-third-country rule for asylum; faster removals; health checks; amend human rights law as needed. No quotas.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Replace CAP with guaranteed minimum prices/deficiency payments; cut bureaucracy; back local abattoirs/markets; support green/organic and hill farms; consider Milk Marketing Board revival.  
- Exit CFP; regain control of UK waters; rebuild protection fleet; conservation via gear rules and fallow zones.

Defence and foreign affairs
- Deploy forces only in the national interest; remain in NATO; leave EU defence structures; reverse cuts; buy British where possible; keep independent voice in the UN.

Energy, environment, transport
- Energy: Stop wind turbine rollout; build new nuclear (fission) and pursue fusion; develop clean coal.  
- Environment: Set UK-led rules; prioritise recycling; protect green belt and habitats; ban GM crops until proven safe.  
- Transport: Invest in roads; resist EU road/rail directives; consider reintegrating rail track and train; continue rail upgrades; local control of traffic; review speed limits; limit speed cameras to safety hotspots.

Governance and society
- Uphold Parliament, monarchy, common law, and an independent House of Lords; allow “English days” at Westminster; scrap English regional assemblies; return business rates/transfer duties to councils; cut “politically correct” posts.  
- Repeal the Human Rights Act; oppose ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act.  
- Reject the “regulatory/compensation culture”; promote responsibility, family, free speech, and smaller, more effective government.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_G better reflects what these voters cared about.
